bullets.title: NVDA: CEO Huang espionage probe creates governance risk; stock -5% while AI trade rallies
bullets.body: NVDA fell ~5% as Jensen Huang's admitted affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset triggered an internal company investigation and DoJ referral (after Commerce Dept paused its Megaspeed probe). The key risk flagged is lack of succession planning — major investors are rushing to support Huang and prediction markets show low probability of his exit, but analysts note China revenue exposure via Singapore is likely contained and the broader AI trade rallied sharply despite NVDA headlines.

bullets.title: AMD: Oppenheimer upgrades to Outperform; semis +6.9% ex-NVDA on AI rotation
bullets.body: AMD surged 13.3% after Oppenheimer upgraded the stock to Outperform from Perform, with semis broadly +6.9% on the day as investors rotated into NVDA alternatives. KeyBanc's Cloud Instance Tracker showed AMD Turin +4% m/m to 4,616 instances with combined Turin/Genoa growth +2% m/m, with analysts viewing AMD implications as positive.

bullets.title: TTD: Massive 3Q beat and $731M buyback drives +23% AH surge; Citi stays Sell at $11 PT
bullets.body: Trade Desk reported 3Q revenue of $736M (13% above guidance/consensus) and adj. EBITDA of $265.8M (36.1% margin, 65% above consensus); 4Q guidance of at least $755M revenue and $280M EBITDA came in 10% and 45% above consensus respectively, and the board authorized an additional $731M buyback bringing total available to $1B. Despite the blowout, Citi maintains Sell with an $11 PT (~5x 2027 EV/EBITDA), citing visibility challenges, macro headwinds, management changes, and DSP competition — implying 26% downside from current $14.93.

bullets.title: APP: eCommerce store growth accelerates to 3% w/w in 4Q; Citi Buy
bullets.body: AppLovin's global eCommerce client count reached 21,011 as of Nov 6 (+3.1% w/w), with US stores at 7,018 growing 3.0% w/w — an acceleration from the 1.5% average weekly growth in 3Q26. 4Q26 YTD average weekly store growth has accelerated to 6.0%, implying an average store count of ~23K for the quarter vs ~11.9K in 3Q26; Citi maintains Buy.

bullets.title: Data center REITs: Buy-the-dip consensus across EQIX, DLR, WULF, CRWV; sector +3.83%
bullets.body: Cantor Fitzgerald, Wells Fargo, and Morgan Stanley all recommend buying the recent selloff in data center names — Cantor maintains Overweight on EQIX, DLR, HUT, WULF, NBIS, CRWV; Wells favors DLR, WULF, APLD, HUT; MS recommends selective buys in EQIX and powered-shell providers. Morgan Stanley's global thematic note argues midterm election impact on capex is overblown — only ~20% of US projects shift from 2028 to 2029 — with hyperscaler capex forecasts unchanged at $1.6T/$1.8T in 2027/2028, and a >30% powered data center shortfall through 2028 favoring largest operators.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Launches TPU 8tx and 8i Max chips; AVGO-designed Blade Runner TPU anticipated
bullets.body: Google introduced two new TPU AI chips focused on confidential computing and longer context windows, per JPM's afternoon briefing. AVGO-designed Blade Runner TPU is also anticipated. GOOGL was cited as a key beneficiary in MS's 'buy the drop' AI note alongside META, AMZN, and MSFT.

bullets.title: META: +5.1% leading hyperscaler rally; building enterprise sales force ahead of monetization meeting
bullets.body: META surged 5.1% despite CSO Dave Wehner departing for Fireworks AI, leading the hyperscaler group as JPM highlighted it ahead of an upcoming monetization meeting and noted the company is building an enterprise sales force. MS's AI thematic note flagged META targeting 10x compute efficiency improvement in 2027 through model distillation.

bullets.title: DLR: Acquires 9.9% of NextDC with Goodman Group for ~$500M APAC expansion; Citi Buy, $234 PT
bullets.body: Digital Realty and Goodman Group acquired a 9.9% stake (~$500M) in NextDC to broaden APAC data center footprint; DLR's retail-centric Australian portfolio complements its global hyperscale exposure. Citi maintains Buy with $234 PT based on DCF (2030 revenue $13.7B, 44% EBITDA margin, 8.6% WACC) and projects 3-year Cash NOI CAGR of 17.0% through 2030.

bullets.title: WBD/Skydance: 3Q EBITDA beat but Q4 Studio profits guided $200M lower on Warner Bros. slate miss
bullets.body: Skydance reported 3Q adjusted EBITDA of $1.0B, beating UBS's $937M estimate, on revenues of $7.03B in line with guidance. However, management guided Q4 Studio profits $200M below prior expectations due to Warner Bros. film slate underperformance, while DTC growth and TV trends remain consistent; UBS maintains Sell.

bullets.title: FOXA: Upgraded to Buy at Seaport ($76 PT); Roku deal closes, coverage dropped by UBS/Wolfe
bullets.body: Fox Corp completed its acquisition of Roku on November 6, with ROKU shares delisted from NASDAQ — UBS and Wolfe Research both ceased coverage. Separately, Seaport Research Partners upgraded FOXA to Buy from Neutral with a $76 PT; FOXA entered an $8.4B bridge credit facility for the Roku deal and increased its term loan to $2B.

bullets.title: WULF: Citi Buy, PT cut to $24 on higher WACC; AI/HPC leasing on track
bullets.body: Citi lowered its WULF price target from prior level to $24, citing estimate revisions and a WACC increase from 9% to 10%, while maintaining Buy. The company is executing on leasing ramp, power portfolio expansion, and credit backstop establishment; WULF is trading at an implied 8% cap rate on its contracted opportunity with strong customer interest for AI/HPC data center capacity.

bullets.title: ORCL: OCI site political headwinds mixed post-midterms; KeyBanc Overweight maintained
bullets.body: KeyBanc maintains Overweight on ORCL, noting November 4 election results were net-negative for Oracle's OCI build but reversal risk on five mega-sites in flight (two Texas, one Wisconsin, one Michigan, one New Mexico) is 'extremely low.' New Mexico presents the most risk with two anti-data-center county commissioners elected; KeyBanc forecasts ORCL revenue at $90.9B in 2027E and $126.8B in 2028E.

bullets.title: CSCO/DELL/ANET: Citi hardware roundtable bullish post-correction; ANET preferred over CLS
bullets.body: Citi's TMT hardware roundtable is constructive on DELL, CSCO, and ANET after the recent selloff. CSCO has derisked gross margins with potential for hyperscaler guidance upside from $7.5B to $8B+; DELL near-term guidance seen as conservative with improved setup; ANET slightly preferred over CLS by the majority. Key risk: potential H2:27/2028 capex cuts due to regulatory impacts being haircut in expectations.

bullets.title: ARM: Cloud instances +11% m/m, +43% y/y led by Google Axion; KeyBanc views as positive
bullets.body: KeyBanc's Cloud Instance Tracker showed ARM instances surging +11% m/m and +43% y/y, driven by Google Axion +26% m/m and Azure Cobalt +15% m/m. NVDA instances fell -6% m/m as Pascal regions dropped 34% at GCP and BABA, while Blackwell only gained +1% m/m; AMD and INTC implications also viewed positively.

bullets.title: CEG/VST/NNE/OKLO/BE: Power & nuclear names surge; CEG raises FY26 EPS 5% to $12.65
bullets.body: CEG jumped 10.5% after Q3 beat and raising FY26 EPS midpoint 5% to $12.65 with 4,560 MWs of contracting signed in the quarter. OKLO +14%, NNE +12.3% on alternative energy demand; BE +12% on improved outlook with RBC maintaining Outperform at $335 PT. FSLR underperformed -4.7% as solar lagged the broader renewables rally.

bullets.title: DIS: +2.0% on multi-year Adobe AI alliance; Disney+ evolving into digital hub with UGC and free ad tier
bullets.body: Disney rose 2.0% on announcement of a multi-year strategic alliance with Adobe for custom AI in innovation labs, alongside plans to evolve Disney+ into a digital hub featuring user-generated content and an ad-supported free tier. ADBE was cited as the partner; both names were among the day's media/comm services gainers.

bullets.title: SNAP: Director Robert Murphy files Form 144 for potential sale of 2.0M shares at $5.05
bullets.body: Snap director and co-founder Robert Murphy filed a Form 144 notice for the potential sale of 2.0M shares through Wells Fargo at a stock price of $5.05 — a routine insider sale notice but notable given the size relative to Snap's float.

bullets.title: JPM: SPX target 8,000 YE26; 10 bullish catalysts with AI multiples compressed 35%+ since May
bullets.body: JPM reiterates its YE26 SPX target of 8,000 (8.4% upside) on $365 EPS at 21.9x, citing 10 bullish catalysts: clean positioning, depressed sentiment, RSI oversold (NDX at 30), valuations derated 3x since May, incoming buybacks, and lower yields. AI multiples have compressed 35% since May (Semis -52%, Memory -60%), levered ETF sales dropped exposure below Jan 2026 levels, and ~$50B of CTA selling remains.

bullets.title: MSFT: Annual Fall HQ Visit at Jefferies Nov 12; ongoing AI infrastructure beneficiary
bullets.body: Jefferies is hosting a Microsoft Annual Fall Headquarters Visit on November 12 in Redmond — a potential catalyst for updated management commentary on AI infrastructure and enterprise software trends. MSFT was also cited in MS's 'buy the drop' AI thematic note as a core hyperscaler holding.

bullets.title: DKNG: Participating in Jefferies Digital Gaming Summit Dec 3 in NYC
bullets.body: DraftKings IR team (Matt Gaudioso and Matt Rappaport) will be participating in the Jefferies Digital Gaming Summit on December 3 in NYC for 1x1 and small group meetings. Request deadline is November 17 — a potential channel-check opportunity ahead of Q4.
